catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class fits a fixed-channel timing-trigger enable/disable selection. cap.actuation.gpio.v1 models a general-purpose output pin with a caller-supplied pin number and a numeric value; the TPR channel is fixed when the Device is constructed (pcdsdevices/tpr.py:137-152), and the upstream operation is a pair of enable commands for the channel and the trigger output (pcdsdevices/tpr.py:154-178), not a pin write. The extension action selects channel, trigger or both and calls the exact upstream enable_ch/disable_ch/enable_trg/disable_trg methods; it has an inline input/output schema and no external effect beyond those calls.

notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/pcdshub__pcdsdevices --backend fake; the evidence is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. No hardware was attached, no IOC or Channel Access network was used, and the hardware backend was never opened. This package is authored by deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017 (a model, not a human); reviewed_by is null and no human reviewed or tested it.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's helper is OphydDriver, but the confirmed entry symbol pcdsdevices.tpr:TprTrigger (pcdsdevices/tpr.py:60) builds every signal with FormattedComponent (pcdsdevices/tpr.py:75-132), which the classic-Ophyd direct-Component source proof does not accept. The package is therefore a direct Driver over the card's entry symbol, with native.py as the hardware factory, as driver-authoring.md permits. The primary control is preserved: the upstream enable/disable operations for the channel and trigger (pcdsdevices/tpr.py:154-178) are exposed through x-cap.pcdshub.tpr_trigger.v1, and the trigger delay and width are exposed through their upstream MultiDerivedSignal put/get paths (pcdsdevices/tpr.py:95-101, 117-123).

Covered: reads channel_enabled (enable_ch_cmd.get), trigger_enabled (enable_trg_cmd.get), eventrate (eventrate.get), delay_ns (ns_delay.get), width_ns (width.get) and label (label.get); writes delay_ns through ns_delay.put and width_ns through width.put; one extension action selecting channel, trigger or both through the upstream enable_ch/disable_ch/enable_trg/disable_trg methods; @estop calls the native TprTrigger.disable(), which disables the channel then the trigger; the runtime latches and refuses the action and writes until an operator reset. test_driver.py keeps check_driver and adds cases for the reads, both writes, the operator-required refusal, an out-of-envelope refusal, the extension action and the e-stop.

Limits: no text of the clone states a trigger-delay or trigger-width range; ns_delay and width are derived signals over tick/tap/setpoint PVs (pcdsdevices/tpr.py:13-16, 95-101, 117-123), so delay_ns and width_ns use Limit.operator_required with that reason. site-limits.example.json supplies illustrative 0..100000 ns bounds so the conformance suite can exercise the paths; those numbers are example test data, are not sourced facts or device limits, and must be replaced by the installed timing system's ranges before hardware use. eventrate carries no unit because the clone states none.

NOT COVERED: ns_delay_scan (the TprMotor PV positioner), count, and the many configuration signals of the class, including ratemode, group, seqcode, fixedrate, destmask, destmode, src, eventcode, delay_ticks, delay_taps, delay_setpoint, polarity, width_setpoint, width_ticks and operation; the timing-mode and prefix are deployment inputs of native.py rather than served state. The full TPR Device has a larger signal surface than this package serves.

Safety: risk R1, the card's floor and the class's software trigger-control scope; this is a TTL timing trigger, not a laser, high-voltage contact, high-force actuator or robot. The clone declares no independent hardware e-stop for the class, so no estop_physical_ref is claimed. The e-stop is a software latch plus the native disable commands; disabling the channel and trigger is not evidence that downstream lasers, shutters or detectors stopped, and no pulse-absence readback is exposed. The fake disable path was exercised; no hardware stop was observed.

Hardware backend: native.py imports pcdsdevices.tpr only when an operator loads the hardware backend; the operator must supply the PV prefix and channel (documented 0 through 11 at pcdsdevices/tpr.py:71-72) and LCLS1 or LCLS2 timing mode; it constructs TprTrigger and waits for connection once, for at most connection_timeout_s (0, 60] s. It requires the pcdsdevices, ophyd and pyepics installation and a live EPICS timing IOC; it was never run.

Gate notes: the run printed no warnings; G1-G9 all passed. The site overlay is example-only and narrows the operator-required writes; the package's facts and refs were checked against commit d13b06eb53e6185088a7534ce0e17ab154463407.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the direct-Driver deviation against the readiness evidence (blocked as carded: OphydDriver cannot prove TprTrigger's FormattedComponents, tpr.py:75-132; a direct Driver over the class is allowed and serves its primary control, the channel and trigger enables, delay and width), R1, the operator-required limits, every fact, native.py and the stop. Defects: the e-stop's disable() is a plain put(0) with no wait or callback (tpr.py:159-178) and the e-stop returned at once, so a completed e-stop proved nothing; the writes went through ns_delay.put/width.put, whose utils.set_many logs and drops an exception of the member set and returns a finished Status (utils.py:556-579), so a failed setpoint write could be reported completed; the fake stored the written number in ns_delay and width and the tests asserted the read returned it, while upstream the put writes only the setpoint (_put_last, tpr.py:34-36) and the read is computed from tick and tap PVs (24-31); two facts said more than their lines (TimingMode selection on 19-21, the delay formula on 13-16). The reviewer made the e-stop read both enable commands back and raise SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED unless both are 0, made each write call set on the same setpoint member (delay_setpoint, width_setpoint) with a 5 s timeout and wait on its Status, rewrote safe_state, the docstring and the write descriptions, corrected the two facts and added six (formulas, _put_last, setpoint PVs, AggregateSignal.get, MultiDerivedSignal.put/set, set_many) (driver.py); made ns_delay and width derived fakes over placeholder tick, tap and setpoint members (fake.py); changed the read and write cases and added three (a failed set fails the write, the derived formulas, an unconfirmed disable leaves the e-stop unreached with the latch held) (test_driver.py); updated facts.md (with a licence note) and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate passes with the digest unchanged (sha256:9e4be3e07a9024c50d2133d4f94029ac663ffad55072812204ce8f1a08a1bb22); the author's notes on the ns_delay.put/width.put writes and on the e-stop are superseded. For the human reviewer: TPR timing trigger at R1: what the channel fires decides a deployment's real hazard (a laser, Pockels cell or pulsed high-voltage system raises the risk), and enabling the channel or trigger fires that equipment. The e-stop's readback confirms the IOC's enable records, not the absence of pulses, and other channels keep firing. Enable puts pass no wait or callback; reads call get() without use_monitor, so their freshness follows the deployment's ophyd defaults.
